A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TikZero. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, training ablations, a human evaluation and supplementary inverse-graphics experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds baseline evaluations and a probe/gate ablation in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, distillation losses, training stages and inference procedures remain unchanged. TikZero (Base) is introduced as an ablation removing existing components, rather than a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DaTikZv3 and ArxivCap coverage and retain caption-to-program, reference-image and synthetic-sketch evaluations. The additional models are evaluated within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix A and Table 5 add Qwen2.5 Coder (14B), DeepSeek-R1 Qwen (14B) and DeepSeek-R1 Qwen (32B), while retaining existing comparators. This substantially broadens comparison to reasoning models and adds a smaller coding-model comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds a controlled configuration that jointly removes the trainable probe and gating mechanism. Existing evaluation settings, including the 1,000-example test split, metrics, sampling temperature and top-p, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix A tests the combined contribution of the probe and gates by comparing TikZero (Base) with TikZero (Cos). This is one additional architectural ablation; the fine-tuning, typographic-attack, low-resource and inverse-graphics analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Human-evaluation annotation counts and split-half reliability reporting remain unchanged. v3 adds no model-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests; the additional table also reports point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 2–4 and the matched older appendix results are unchanged. New Table 5 adds four configurations: for example, TikZero (Base) scores 52.373 on DreamSim and 9.428 on CLIPScore, versus 52.829 and 10.051 for TikZero (Cos). Section 5.3 also explicitly reports rho = 1.0 for both human-versus-metric system rankings.

T1.justification: The distillation objective in Equation 1 and EMD formulation in Equation 2 are unchanged. The latter moves from Appendix A to B; no new assumptions, derivations or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: decoupled zero-shot synthesis, DaTikZv3 and enhanced TikZero+ performance. The additional experiments support existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: New Appendix A interprets the joint ablation as supporting the probe/gate design and the reasoning-model results as suggesting that reasoning alone is insufficient without domain-specific post-training. Existing interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds document-class declarations to all four Figure 6 code listings, completing their previously incomplete preambles. Existing training details, hardware, inference prompt and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Palatucci et al. on zero-shot learning, OpenAI's reasoning work and DeepSeek-R1. Research positioning expands modestly to reasoning-model comparisons; other reference edits mainly update publication metadata or consolidate a duplicate citation.

P1.justification: There are localized abstract, introduction and method wording edits, affiliation corrections and a new opening appendix section. Existing appendix letters and cross-references are updated, while the main section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 5, relocates the architecture diagram from page 4 to page 3 and rearranges appendix displays. Existing figures and tables largely retain their visual design and content; Figure 6 listings gain the missing preamble lines.

improvement.justification: The added baselines broaden empirical support, the joint ablation directly checks an architectural choice, and completed code preambles improve reproducibility. These are useful but limited gains: core results remain unchanged, and the ablation neither separates the two components' effects nor reports uncertainty for its small differences.
